name: riichiprac whole-table 3D reference
status: Calibration-only. One authoritative Blender scene of the complete table, for comparing the opt-in 2.5D compositor's pieces against a single physical perspective. It is not a runtime dependency, it does not replace the compositor, and nothing under frontend/public is written by this pipeline.

sourceOfTruth.shells: frontend/public/table/shells.json (measured face/back colours and body sizes the reference is checked against)
sourceOfTruth.faces: frontend/public/table/faces/<id>.png (the same perspective-neutral glyph masters the runtime atlas uses)
sourceOfTruth.note: The reference imports the shell baker's tile mesh, one-material white/blue gate and tile proportions, so the reference body cannot drift from the shipped shells.

table.units: tile units: 1 unit = the 28 mm tile height, the same scale as shell-spec.json (0.75 wide, 0.58929 thick)
table.origin: table centre at (0, 0, 0); the human sits on -Y; +Z is up

wall.note: Each run is 17 stacks with a 0.3 mm gap (pitch 0.760714), two face-down tiles high with a 0.3 mm tier gap, ring radius 7.0. Corners keep a small clearance, so no wall tiles intersect. Every wall has one tile missing on the top tier at slot 16 (the draw end); the bottom tile remains. The draw end is the close side of the left wall, the left of the top wall, the far side of the right wall and the right of the close wall (clockwise drawing).

deadWall.note: The west (left) wall has the 7-stack dead wall at slots 0..6 with a 0.5-unit break after slot 6; the live wall is slots 7..16. The dora indicator is the face-up top tile at slot 4. The dead-wall seats use the same wall_seat_stack_layer anchors.

pond.note: 18 discards per pond in three 6-wide rows with a 0.2 mm column gap and a 0.3 mm row gap. Row 0 is nearest the discarding player (radius 4.81) and the rows advance toward the table centre; row 2 is at 2.7886 so the four inner pond rows clear each other at the corners. The pond outer edge (5.31) leaves 1.19 units to the wall inner edge, so the two-tier wall does not occlude the visible near row at 45 deg. Four overflow anchors continue row 2 at columns 6..9 (reserved; no tiles).

riichi.note: One riichi discard per pond, the last tile of row 1; rotated 90 deg to the declaring player's right (glyph top to the seat's right). The turned tile is wider along the row, so it is shifted after the previous tile and marked turned.

hand.note: A standing 13-tile row with a 0.3 mm gap. The human's (south) hand is reclined 12 deg backward about its far bottom edge, blue back to the table centre; the other three hands are upright back rows. The human also gets a separate 14th draw slot at +5.5805 (the intentional tsumogiri gap, not the 0.3 mm row clearance); opponents have 13 anchors.

meld.note: One four-slot meld row per seat OUTSIDE the wall ring, on the table edge at the hand's radius 10.6, to the right of the player's hand (x from 6.1, clear of the drawn tile at x 5.58). Slots 0 and 1 are upright (0.75 wide), slot 2 is the called tile lying sideways (1.0 wide) and slot 3 is the kan extension; the modelled pon occupies slots 0-2 and slot 3 is an anchor only.

playingMat.note: 700 mm x 700 mm playable mat, built as a square ring with a 4.0-unit compass well in the centre; the mat top is z = 0.

rim.note: Raised outer frame around the 700 mm mat, 0.9 units (25 mm) wide and 0.35 units (9.8 mm) high.

floor.note: Dark floor under the mat/rim, replacing the old full-bleed felt plane.

compassWell.note: Recessed centre compass/score well: a 4.0-unit square hole in the mat, a dark floor at -0.06, a near-black plate and a brass ring. Everything is below z = 0, so it cannot occlude a pond or a wall.

body.note: Slab under the mat and rim; its top is just below z=0 so the mat is the tile contact plane.

camera.note: One perspective camera for the whole table at the pond/wall shells' 45 deg elevation, so a centre pond tile projects to the same ~103 px body long axis as the 104 px @1x shells. 'weak' is the committed framing: a long lens at more than twice the physical eye distance, which keeps the near/far tile scale spread close to the compositor's deliberately uniform scale while each zone still shows a real lateral reveal. It is the 2.5D compromise made explicit.

output.note: @1x is the shell scale: a centre pond tile's projected long axis is ~100 px, the same ballpark as shells.json's 104 px base. The 700 mm mat plus its raised rim needs a taller frame than the felt-only scene, so the board is 2880x2112 (1.364:1) from one 5760x4224 @2x master; the eye, lens, elevation and scale are unchanged. The 2x master is rendered once and both the 1x board and the 2x crops are derived from it.

ortho.note: No convergence and no lateral reveal at all. The audit case: it proves how much of the table read is the elevation plus thickness rather than perspective.

physical.note: A strong-perspective audit case: 65 mm at the physical eye distance (57.4 units), 45 deg elevation. It shows the largest near/far size spread and the strongest lateral reveal.

lighting.convention: One global key at the shell bake's screen-space top-left reference direction (azimuth 315 fronts -X/-Y, elevation 55), but as a distant sun so the whole table is lit evenly instead of the near corner being several stops brighter than the far one. Shadows fall down-right on screen, matching the compositor's blob offset. The sun strength is tuned so a bare 5z (haku) face measures the shipped shell's face colour.

rig.name: 2.5D perspective camera + lighting rig
rig.status: Task 2 of 2_5d_implementation_plan.md. Same scene and the same 269 tile placements as the placement reference; the --rig render mode swaps in this camera and light rig, hides the room floor and writes the 16:9 gameplay framing with a transparent film so the published PNG is clean RGBA. Calibration-only: nothing under frontend/public is written and the runtime never reads it.

camera.note: Perspective, 75 mm on a 36 mm sensor, pitched 50 deg down from horizontal, centred on X = 0 behind the south edge at 76 units. 76 units is the distance at which the whole 700 mm mat plus rim fits the 16:9 width with a comfortable ~165 px margin each side and the far rim still inside the frame. Blender's Shift Y is measured against the sensor width, and its positive direction moves the image down; Shift Y -0.02 therefore raises the image 38.4 px, which buys the far rim its headroom and leaves the player's standing hand 74 px above the bottom edge without pitching the camera further down. shiftX = 0 and no roll keep every world-vertical edge parallel to the screen vertical up to the small outward convergence the 50 deg pitch produces (about 2.3 px at the outer hand slots, measured and gated by check-table-rig.mjs); a pitched camera cannot give exactly parallel verticals, and a level camera cannot see the table.

lighting.convention: A large soft overhead AREA key slightly forward of table centre (toward the camera) plus three low-intensity AREA fills, one from the near/south side for the standing hand and two low side fills for the side-wall inner vertical faces. Cycles path-traced GI supplies the contact occlusion and soft shadows under the tile bases (there is no Eevee AO toggle in the Cycles engine). The key is neutral warm and the fills are cool so the bevels and inner faces read against the ivory body without tinting the face paint.

key.note: 20 x 14 units (560 x 392 mm) at 22 units up, 2.5 units forward of centre; the source is large enough that tile-base contact shadows are soft penumbrae rather than a hard stamp.

fills.note: Near/south fill: lights the player's standing hand fronts and the south-facing inner faces of the far wall; cool and low so it only opens the shadows.
Left side fill: defines the west wall's inner vertical faces and the left bevels.
Right side fill: mirrors the left fill for the east wall's inner vertical faces and the right bevels.

world.note: Ambient sky at the shell baker's world tint, low strength; with film transparent it still lights the scene but does not write a background.

ambientOcclusion.note: Cycles path-traced global illumination produces the soft contact shadow under every tile base and the crevice darkening between neighbours; no post AO pass and no Eevee AO setting exists in this engine.

render.colorManagement: table-reference scene block (sRGB, AgX, AgX - Medium High Contrast, exposure 0)
render.note: Film > Transparent plus the room floor hidden: the published PNG is RGBA with a transparent surround, so the board can be composited and the alpha is a checkable fact. The mat, rim, centre well and every tile stay opaque. 64 samples with adaptive sampling and OpenImageDenoise is the smallest count that leaves the bevelled edges clean at 1920 x 1080.

samples.note: Pixel probes for the lighting facts. The pond's 5z face (the faces.sampleTileId) and the wall's blue back are the same probes the placement reference uses, so the rig can be compared with the shipped shells. hand-bottom-06 is forced to 5z in the rig scene only, giving a known blank ivory hand face (the near-fill read). The side probes average the pixels inside each side wall's projected inner vertical face (a single pixel would spill at 3.8 px wide). matWorldPoint is open felt between the north pond and the north wall: the north wall stands farther from the camera, so it cannot occlude the probe, and the point is clear of tile shadows (the near strip behind the south wall is occluded by the wall's own top at a 50 deg pitch).

southWallFace.note: A row of probes on the south wall's outer vertical face at z = 0.1, inside and outside the player's hand span (the hand covers |x| <= 5). The hand's fill shadow on this wall is the give-away the shadow cheat removes, so the checker compares the centre probe with the two end probes: a uniform row (small dip) means nothing is cast on the wall. Informational for variants without the cheat.

handShadow.note: Felt probes south of the player's hand's front edge, on the mat at x = 0: 50, 150, 250, 400 and 600 thousandths of a unit from the tile's front edge. The last is the local lit-felt reference; a gradient shadow must stay above a floor at the closest probe and be essentially gone by the fade distance. Informational for variants without a decal.

checks.note: Thresholds are the acceptance criteria of the plan's Task 2, in numbers: perspective + 75 mm + 50 deg + X = 0 + negative shift, the full table width inside the frame, the south hand near the bottom, no inward vertical lean and at most maxOutwardLeanPx of outward lean, side-wall inner faces at least wallInnerFaceMinPx wide, the centre hand tile straight-on and the outer hand tiles showing a sliver, and a lit ivory face / blue back / readable hand face / lit inner side face in the render.

output.note: The plan's reference resolution. One render per variant, not a @2x master: the rig is a perspective/lighting calibration target, and Task 3 exports normalized screen coordinates and quads, not pixels from a board. Committed variants live together under reference/rig/ so they can be A/B compared; {variant} is the variant id.

v1-baseline.label: v1 baseline (committed 2026-11-17)
v1-baseline.note: The first committed rig: whole table width framed with the near rim as the working-area border, the hand reclined 12 deg, 75 mm at 76 units, 9000 W key. Saved unchanged as the A/B reference.

v2-compact.label: v2 compact + readable hand + dimmer key
v2-compact.note: The user's 2026-11-17 direction: everything bigger and more compact, hands and melds pulled in to the wall, the player's hand reclined further so the faces read from the 50 deg camera (a deliberate cheat; the runtime will use a blob shadow under it, not this render's real shadow), and the key dimmed so the discards stop reading as blown-out white. The mat/rim are only the working-area border and are allowed to crop.

hand.note: v2: 13 standing tiles with a 0.3 mm gap, pulled in to radius 8.8 (v1: 10.6) so the row sits 1.3 units behind the wall's outer edge (v1: 3.1). The 14th draw slot keeps the tsumogiri gap. The tiles are RECLINED 40 deg about their far bottom edges as a deliberate readability cheat, so the near bottom edge floats 0.38 units above the table and the real cast shadow is not the production shadow (the runtime uses a blob). Their shading normals are corrected to the 12 deg physical pose (see rig.variants['v2-compact'].lightingCheat), so the light on them is the physical read.

meld.note: v2: one four-slot meld row per seat at the hand's new radius 8.8 (v1: 10.6), to the right of the player's hand; the drawn tile ends at x 5.58 and the row starts at x 6.1. Slots 0-1 upright, slot 2 the called tile lying sideways, slot 3 the kan extension.

camera.note: v2 experiment: framed to the tile content (hands at radius 8.8, melds at 8.8) rather than the 700 mm mat, so the tiles read ~1.29x larger than v1 in linear size (~1.68x in area). 59 units leaves every tile inside the frame (>=27 px) with the hand 45 px above the bottom edge; the mat and rim are only the working-area border and the rim crosses the frame edges. Blender's Shift Y convention is unchanged from v1 (negative raises the image).

key.note: v2: dimmed from the 9000 W baseline so the discard faces stop reading as blown-out white. Same position, size and colour.

fills.note: Near/south fill: lights the player's standing hand fronts and the south-facing inner faces of the far wall; cool and low so it only opens the shadows.
Left side fill: defines the west wall's inner vertical faces and the left bevels.
Right side fill: mirrors the left fill for the east wall's inner vertical faces and the right bevels.

lightingCheat.note: The hand's geometry keeps the 40 deg cheat so the faces read, but every hand material shades with its normal rotated back by the extra 28 deg about world X, so the key and fills land on it exactly as they would on the 12 deg physical pose. The illusion is the point: the viewer should not read the tilt as a lighting change. The real cast shadow is still the cheated pose's; the runtime will use a blob shadow instead.

v3-hand-shadow.label: v3 compact + player hand back + physical hand shadow
v3-hand-shadow.note: The user's follow-up on v2: only the player's hand moves a further half tile height back from the wall, and its shadow stops giving the cheat away. The cheated hand casts no shadow at all (no tall shadow under it, nothing up the wall behind it); each hand tile gets a shadow-only caster at the 12 deg physical pose, and the fills are light-linked to ignore the caster, so only the key casts a short, diffuse physical shadow. The rest of the table is v2.

hand.note: v3: the shared 8.8 radius applies to the three opponent hands; only the player's (bottom) hand moves back to 9.3, a further half tile height (0.5 units) from the wall. The player's drawn tile moves with it. The tilt stays the 40 deg readability cheat, shaded as the 12 deg physical pose.

handShadow.note: The cheated hand bodies and decals are invisible to shadow rays. Each body is duplicated at the 12 deg physical pose as a shadow-only caster: invisible to the camera, diffuse and glossy rays, and volume scatter, visible only to shadow rays. The fills are light-linked to a blocker collection that omits the casters, so only the key (69 deg above, north of the hand) casts the shadow: a short band falling south, like the shadow in front of the wall, and nothing on the wall behind.

camera.note: v3: refit after moving the player's hand back to radius 9.3; 60.5 units keeps every tile inside the frame (>=28 px) with the hand 29 px above the bottom edge. Same 75 mm / 50 deg / X = 0 / Shift Y -0.02 as v2.

lightingCheat.note: v3: the hand's geometry keeps the 40 deg cheat so the faces read, and every hand material still shades as the 12 deg physical pose. Unlike v2, the cast shadow is now also the physical pose's (rig.variants['v3-hand-shadow'].handShadow), so the shading and the shadow both read as a normally seated tile.

v4-shadow-decal.label: v4 soft gradient hand shadow
v4-shadow-decal.note: v4 keeps v3's spacing (the player's hand at 9.3) and replaces the rendered physical-pose caster with a fake soft gradient decal: the v3 caster read as hard black rectangles that started at the rear edge where the tile balances. The decal is a straight-alpha black strip laid on the mat whose darkest point is hidden under the tile and whose visible gradient begins right at the tile's front edge, as if the tile sat upright and level, then fades to nothing within a third of a tile height. It casts no shadow rays, so the wall behind stays clean.

handShadow.note: A short gradient strip per hand group (the 13-tile row and the drawn tile). startRadius = frontEdge - edgeHeight/tan(pitch) so the hard near edge sits under the tile and the first visible pixels are already part of the falloff. maxAlpha 0.3 keeps the darkest visible mat at ~70% of the lit felt; the falloff (1-v)^1.2 returns to lit felt inside 0.32 units (~9 mm).

v5-shadow-wash.label: v5 shadow wash — 0.55 units, alpha 0.50
v5-shadow-wash.note: Shadow take A: a medium-long, evenly fading wash. About 0.55 units (15 mm) of gradient, roughly 45 % dark at the visible edge, back to lit felt before the frame edge. This is the 'a bit longer, clearly visible' reading of v4.

camera.note: Shadow take: the framing lifts 19 px (Shift Y -0.03 instead of -0.02) so the longer gradient has lit felt below it and never reaches the frame edge. Everything else is v4.

handShadow.note: Shadow take: the same hidden-start gradient as v4, longer and more visible.

v6-shadow-long-faint.label: v6 long faint shadow — 0.65 units, alpha 0.40
v6-shadow-long-faint.note: Shadow take B: the longest and softest. About 0.65 units (18 mm), a light even haze (about 35 % dark at the edge) that fades slowly. This is the most diffuse take and the least 'contact shadow'.

camera.note: Shadow take: the framing lifts 19 px (Shift Y -0.03 instead of -0.02) so the longer gradient has lit felt below it and never reaches the frame edge. Everything else is v4.

handShadow.note: Shadow take: the same hidden-start gradient as v4, longer and more visible.

v7-shadow-deep.label: v7 deep contact shadow — 0.42 units, alpha 0.65
v7-shadow-deep.note: Shadow take C: the deepest but shortest. About 0.42 units (12 mm), roughly 55 % dark at the visible edge and dropping quickly, so it reads as a firmer contact shadow rather than a wash.

camera.note: Shadow take: the framing lifts 19 px (Shift Y -0.03 instead of -0.02) so the longer gradient has lit felt below it and never reaches the frame edge. Everything else is v4.

handShadow.note: Shadow take: the same hidden-start gradient as v4, longer and more visible.

v10-shadow-split-blobs.label: v10 split blobs, blurred on all four edges
v10-shadow-split-blobs.note: Take A (v5) rebuilt with the retired UI shadow recipe, then corrected: the contact rectangle is blurred on all four edges (v9's hard north cut left a sharp line past the end tiles), each group widens only outward (the row's left, the drawn tile's right) so the tsumogiri gap keeps the drawn tile's blob separate, and the row/drawn planes are staggered to stop them z-fighting. Same spacing, framing, lighting and hand cheat as v5.

handShadow.note: A rounded contact rectangle blurred once on all four edges: sigma 0.28 across the depth (take A's long fade) and 0.12 across x, so the row and the drawn tile stay separate at the tsumogiri gap instead of merging. Each group widens only outward (row left / drawn right) by 0.15 units and extends 0.5 units north under the tiles, so the wrap is soft in every direction and never a hard line.

v11-shadow-inner-offset.label: v11 shadow: inner-right extended, offset forward
v11-shadow-inner-offset.note: v10's row shadow stopped at the row's right edge. v11 gives each group its own spreads: the hand row widens both ends by 0.15 units (so its right shadow passes the last tile), the drawn tile widens only outward (0.28 units, well past the hand) and keeps its gap side at its tile edge, so the tsumogiri gap still dips between the two blobs. The whole footprint is offset 0.06 units forward (south) so the shadow does not look like it surrounds the tiles perfectly evenly; the x blur is 0.10.

handShadow.note: One blurred contact rectangle per group, all four edges (sigma 0.28 depth / 0.10 x), 0.5 alpha on every edge. Spreads per group: hand row 0.15 both ends, drawn tile 0 left / 0.28 right; the whole rect is offset 0.06 units south and its north edge sits 0.5 units under the tiles.

v12-shadow-symmetric.label: v12 symmetric per-group shadows, drawn tile centred
v12-shadow-symmetric.note: The v11 shadow double-darkened where the row's and drawn tile's decals overlapped, and the drawn tile's blob was visibly off-centre. v12 applies the retired UI group recipe: the hand row and the drawn tile are unioned into one footprint and blurred once, so there is no overlap darkening and the shadow is symmetric around the whole hand (0.18 units at both outer ends). The drawn tile's shadow is part of the same union rather than a separate off-centre blob; the tsumogiri gap gets shadow like the rest of the union, as the UI recipe does.

handShadow.note: One blurred contact rectangle per group, all four edges (sigma 0.28 depth / 0.10 x), 0.5 alpha on every edge, spread 0.18 on every end so each group's shadow is symmetric around its tiles, the whole rect 0.06 units south, and the north edge 0.5 units under the tiles.

v13-shadow-darker.label: v13 darker hand shadow (match the wall's front shadow)
v13-shadow-darker.note: v12's union shadow was a touch lighter than the key shadow in front of the player's wall (26 luma at its core). v13 keeps the same union footprint, symmetric margins and x blur but darkens it: full black at the core, sigma 0.26, and the footprint offset 0.18 units south, which puts the darkest visible felt at ~27 luma against the wall shadow's 26.

handShadow.note: Same union recipe as v12, darkening only: full black at the core, sigma 0.26, offset 0.09 south so the visible edge sits a little further into the gradient.

faces.note: The glyph masters are composited onto a thin transparent plane 0.001 units above the white plate, exactly the flat 2D glyph the runtime atlas draws, not the carved decal. 5z (haku) has zero ink and gets no plane, which makes it the bare lighting sample tile.

content.note: Every wall stack is face-down. The scene is a visual calibration target, not a legal game state: tile faces are drawn from a seeded shuffle and may repeat more than four times.

naming.river: river_{seat}_{row}_{col}  (row 0..2, col 0..5 plus row-2 overflow cols 6..9)
naming.hand: hand_{seat}_{index:02d}  (index 00..12; south also has 13 for the drawn tile)

faceQuad.space: anchor-local tile units: +x = tile right, +y = glyph top, +z = out of the painted face; the anchor is at the tile's 3D centre
faceQuad.order: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left (glyph image top is +y)
faceQuad.corners: x = +/- (width/2 - faceInset), y = +/- (height/2 - faceInset), z = +thickness/2, with faceInset = 0.055 units (the shell bevel inset)
faceQuad.storage: flat 12-float Blender custom property `faceQuadLocal` on each Empty, plus the published tools/render/reference/slot-anchors.json dump

anchors.note: Every valid tile position is an Empty in the SlotAnchors collection, named wall_{seat}_{stack}_{layer}, river_{seat}_{row}_{col}, meld_{seat}_{slot} or hand_{seat}_{index}. Anchors are at the tile body centre with the tile pose. Occupied anchors hold the 273 reference tiles; the 20 empty anchors are the 16 row-2 overflow slots and 4 kan-extension meld slots. Each anchor carries zone/seat/index/tileId/tileFace/occupied, the flat faceQuadLocal and faceQuadWorld (12 floats, TL/TR/BR/BL) and faceQuadOrder as Blender custom properties; the same records are published in reference/slot-anchors.json. Project anchor.matrix_world @ Vector(faceQuadLocal corner) for Task 3.
